canonical_question: How does the 'Cu matrix' affect the boundary conditions and constraint during the high-temperature deformation?

question_variants.question: How does the 'Cu matrix' affect the boundary conditions and constraint during the high-temperature deformation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text describes the Cu matrix as the substrate material and the HEA as the coating, but does not detail the specific boundary conditions or mechanical constraints imposed by the Cu matrix during high-temperature deformation simulations beyond the layer definition (e.g., 0~5 Å boundary).

answers.answer: The simulation model defines a Cu matrix layer (10~55 Å) adjacent to a high entropy alloy coating, with a boundary layer (0~5 Å) and a constant temperature layer (5~10 Å) used to control thermal conditions, but does not specify the mechanical constraint mechanics imposed by the Cu matrix.
answers.material: Cu matrix / FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating
answers.measurement_outcome: Layer definition: 0~5 Å (boundary), 5~10 Å (constant temperature), 10~55 Å (Cu)
answers.mechanism: Langevin method controls temperature in the constant temperature layer
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit description of mechanical constraint forces from Cu matrix on deformation behavior provided.
evidence_spans: In the nanoindentation model, single crystal Cu was used as the matrix material and FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy was used as the coating material.
The same lattice types of both materials were set.
The model size of the Cu matrix was 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å, and the total number of atoms was 47,111.

source_evidence_spans: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy was used as a coating material to adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix.
